name: kaushal-kalas-portfolio
tagline: A dark, developer-oriented single-page portfolio whose single job is to communicate an AI/ML-focused profile within the first few seconds and make the visit memorable.
description: A dark, developer-oriented single-page portfolio for AI/ML developer Kaushal Kalas. Near-black ink canvas, a single warm amber-gold voltage, and an amber phosphor Debian-style terminal as the signature artifact. Every section wears a $-command eyebrow that maps 1:1 to a working terminal command — the page is the terminal's manual, and the terminal is a shortcut for the page. Structure comes from 1px hairlines dividing dark bands from darker bands, not from stacked shadows; elevation is capped at one shadow tier plus a single terminal glow. Display restraint is the personality of the page.

seed.fontFamilyCode: 'JetBrains Mono', 'SFMono-Regular', Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', Menlo, Courier, monospace

logo.notes: No logo file was supplied in the pasted DESIGN.md. The brand's logo moment is the signal-yellow roundel (28px circle, ink mono 'K') in the nav, plus the terminal prompt line `kaushal@debian:~$ ▊` — the system's type-plus-color lockup. Do not substitute a generated mark.

colors.name: Ink
colors.usage: page canvas (dark floor; near-black with a hair of blue so it never reads warm brown)

colors.name: Surface
colors.usage: cards, terminal chrome, raised fills (1-2 steps off ink; separation comes from hairlines, not brightness)

colors.name: Paper
colors.usage: dominant text on dark — headlines, hero, titles (warm off-white tinted toward the yellow family; ~16:1 on ink)

colors.name: Muted
colors.usage: meta rows, inactive nav, tags, titlebar labels (~6.5:1 on surface)

colors.name: Hairline
colors.usage: default 1px border — section dividers, card borders, terminal outline

colors.name: Primary
colors.usage: warm amber-gold — the single brand color. CTA fills, inline links, active nav, focus rings, nav roundel, terminal prompt prefix. Shifted from pure yellow (#FFD200) to warm amber for dual-theme usability and premium Gen-Z aesthetic; 9.71:1 on ink (AAA), works as button fill on light backgrounds with dark text inside.

colors.name: Primary Active
colors.usage: hover/press step — deeper amber (8.65:1 on ink); used on button hover/active states. Slightly more orange-shifted to communicate depth and interactivity.

display.notes: Wide technical geometric sans. Rationed to the two loud moments: the hero name at weight 700 and one section title per band at 600. Never a body-text role.

body.notes: Neutral modern humanist sans for all running text, cards, and nav. Deliberately quiet.

mono.notes: The machine layer — terminal output, $-eyebrows, meta rows, tags, buttons, dates. If it is data about Kaushal, it is mono; if it is voice, it is Instrument Sans.

voice.tone: Quiet, technical, and self-assured — a Debian manual, not a marketing site. Short machine-precise declaratives; the terminal is the voice and its $ commands are the table of contents. The warm amber accent adds a human glow to the technical precision — luminous, not cold.
messagingPillars: A dark, developer-oriented single-page portfolio whose single job is to communicate an AI/ML-focused profile within the first few seconds and make the visit memorable.

One warm amber-gold voltage (#F5A623) carries every interactive signal: CTAs, links, active nav states, focus rings, and the terminal prompt. There is no second brand color. The orange undertone makes it premium and contemporary — less 'caution tape' than pure yellow, more 'golden hour.'

Dual-theme by design: the amber-gold (#F5A623) is the primary accent on both the ink floor and the paper inversion (engine-verified: the light derivation keeps #F5A623 as primary). On light, amber is structural — button fills with ink text, amber underlines and borders, amber-tinted tags, dark amber eyebrows (#824400) — never full-strength amber as link text. The dark terminal object is unchanged in both themes.

The terminal is the thesis: a Debian-style simulated terminal sits directly under the hero, and every section below opens with a $-command eyebrow that maps 1:1 to a working terminal command — you can scroll or type to the same content.
Structure comes from 1px hairlines dividing dark bands from darker bands, not from stacked shadows; elevation is capped at one shadow tier plus the terminal's dedicated amber glow.
Type is split by role: Unbounded carries the two loud moments (hero name, section titles); Instrument Sans carries the human voice; JetBrains Mono owns everything machine-flavored.

use: $-eyebrows that map 1:1 to working terminal commands
Warm amber-gold (#F5A623) for interactive signals and the terminal prompt only (one or two amber moments per viewport)
JetBrains Mono for machine-flavored content — eyebrows, meta, tags, buttons, the whole terminal
Sentence-case action verbs on button labels ('View projects', 'Download resume')
Terminal output as real DOM text — selectable, copyable, screen-reader-accessible, aria-live='polite'
On light backgrounds: use amber as button fills and border accents with dark text inside, not as link text color
avoid: A second accent color, gradients, or emoji icons
Numbering (01/02/03), percentage skill bars, icon walls
Styling the rest of the site like a terminal — the terminal is an object, not a theme
Fake terminal behavior — no arbitrary command execution, no fake sudo prompts
Animating more than 600ms, or transforming anything but opacity and transform
Amber text on light backgrounds — use amber as fills/borders with dark text instead

imagery.style: Photographic and dark. Every gallery image is a real 4:3 artifact (reserved aspect ratio, object-fit cover, lazy-loaded, caption beneath). The page itself carries no decorative imagery — the amber terminal is the single ornament.
subjects: project screenshots in a reserved 4:3 frame
imagery.treatment: Muted and captioned; hover steps the hairline border toward primary. No zoom, no overlay, no animation — captions stay readable. Meaningful alt text on every image; captions are supplementary, never the only description.
avoid: icons or emoji as functional elements
images with baked-in text or UI chrome
invented metrics, percentage bars, or fake measurements

layout.spacing: 4px base unit (2px micro-step for tag and label gutters); 128px section rhythm on desktop, 72px below 640px
postureRules: Component kit must cover: nav, menu-overlay, button-primary (+ hover/active/disabled), button-secondary (+ hover), terminal-window, terminal-titlebar, terminal-output, prompt-line, project-card, featured-card, card-meta, card-description, tag-chip, section-header, section-eyebrow, divider, divider-soft, gallery-item, contact-row, footer.

Radius language: 2px on tag chips and micro-labels, 4px on interactive elements (buttons, cards, gallery items, terminal output well), 8px on the terminal window only. No pill shapes and no border-radius: 9999px anywhere.
Elevation: one shadow tier (0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.4) card hover) plus the terminal's dedicated glow (0 24px 80px rgba(0,0,0,0.6), 0 0 60px rgba(255,178,0,0.06)). Nothing else casts a shadow.
Single accent: warm amber-gold #F5A623 for every CTA, link, active state, and focus ring — plus the terminal prompt marker. No second brand color; the amber #FFB200 is the terminal phosphor only.

Dark-first canvas: ink #0B0B0C floor with paper #F5F2E8 text is the default; the light inversion (ink ⇄ paper) is shipped as light-theme.html and keeps the amber voltage. On light, amber is structural — button fills/borders with dark text on light backgrounds, never as link text.
Touch targets: primary/secondary CTAs >= 48x48px; contact rows full-width at 48px+; nav links padded to 44px; terminal input 40px min height with up/down history.
Focus: 2px amber-gold outline + 2px offset via :focus-visible on every interactive element — the amber is the focus language of the whole site.

Light-theme amber usage: amber as button background with dark (#0B0B0C) text inside (9.71:1 contrast); amber as underline/border accent on links (not text color); amber focus rings on light (decorative, no contrast requirement).
